conclusion: CODEC(ALP,ZSTD3) vs ZSTD(1) compressed SAMPLES size changes sign across fixed-time/label Float64 distributions, while read CPU tradeoffs remain workload-dependent. No global codec switch.

source.cpu_models: Both independent holdout jobs ran on AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor, 4 logical CPUs each. Original R18 had AMD EPYC 9V45 and R17 AMD EPYC 9V74, so no cross-runner latency comparison.

parent_fixture.source: R01 deterministic aligned synthetic three-day gauges

method: Two new separately SHA-verified fixtures generated from exact parent series: same tags, row ordering, timestamp strings, sample counts, stable RAW UUID IDs and 3600s sample buckets, only Float64 sample values changed. For each fixture, two same-binary tables: stock samples.value CODEC(ALP,ZSTD(3)) vs CODEC(ZSTD(1)), SAMPLES timestamp CODEC(Delta(8),T64,ZSTD(3)), one physical part each. Four full native PromQL selectors, independent ALP/ZSTD/ZSTD/ALP with 2 warmups+8 measured queries each phase. All labels, timestamps and numeric outputs exactly matched per pattern; compare only within each runner and pattern. Physical parts, rows/marks and 2,488,320 elements audited before/after. Both jobs PASS. Write/OPTIMIZE measured once per table, process-wide CPU descriptive only.
findings: ZSTD(1) stores repetitive source values 35.6% smaller than stock ALP SAMPLES, smooth +finely quantized gauges 16.6% smaller, but entropy random doubles **2.7% larger** than ALP; the compressed-size ordering reverses with value entropy on otherwise identical data.

Smooth heldout: node_broad native CPU 375.5->359.5ms (-4.3%) with CPU A/A drift0.4%, burst15 CPU74.2->67.9ms (-8.5%) with drift3.0%. Namespace CPU105.3->95.8ms (-9.0%) but drift5.8%, wall drift10.4%, so less robust than raw delta.

Entropy heldout: pod_namespace native CPU107.8->99.3ms (-7.9%) with A/A CPU drift1.6%, despite ZSTD1 SAMPLES on-disk being larger than ALP. Pod_broad CPU change +5.2% is smaller than 14.3% A/A CPU drift, not robust.

Raw original repetitive fixture: pod_namespace ZSTD1 CPU+10% vs A/A drift0.8% (regression), while smooth/entropy variants have CPU in opposite direction. A single value-codec policy cannot optimize all value shapes and selectors.
Do not use absolute wall/CPU values across original R18 AMD EPYC 9V45 and heldout AMD EPYC 7763. Only same-runner ALP/ZSTD comparisons have matched controls.

Both holdout runs use synthetic labels and timestamps with changed float values; no independent Prometheus semantic oracle beyond same native comparison and no realistic NaN/Inf, resets or out-of-order writes.
limitations: Only 3 days, aligned 400-node gauge-style synthetic data. Entropy uses deterministic SplitMix64 53-bit pseudo-random Float64 in [0,1), smooth range 0.125001-0.127216. Neither is observed production distribution.
Cost of natural repeated inserts, late sample updates, merges and allocation under 8 clients not proven; write/optimize snapshots unpaired.
Stock O1 glibc binary, not optimized jemalloc production parity. JEMALLOC build 41607779848 still running separately at last checkpoint.
ALP/ZSTD effect on dense high-cardinality 14d PromQL exactness, NaN/Inf, staleness, rate and histograms still unknown.
Single representative CPU stack per variant is diagnostic; no named mutex or pure decompression attribution.
next_action: Do not promote a global value-codec default. Use R18 codec source and heldout corpus to estimate a compact production-like histogram of finite Float64 value entropy/quantization, then collect one paired append/merge +8-client read test on representative data if relevant. Avoid repeating synthetic cross-runner performance tests.
